what:
Cursor support gap in `aide-memory init` (2026-04-23, core finding for CURSOR_ONBOARDING plan): `aide-memory init` today writes ONLY `.cursor/rules/aide-memory.mdc` for Cursor users. It does NOT generate `.cursor/hooks.json` (hook registrations) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (MCP server config). The repo's on-disk `.cursor/hooks.json` + `.cursor/mcp.json` are stale legacy artifacts from pre-0.4.0 (they reference the old bash `scripts/hooks/stop-remember.sh`, `detect-correction.sh`, `recall-for-path.js` paths that got consolidated into `dist/cli/aide-memory.js hook <name>` in the 0.4.0 hook consolidation). So Cursor users who run `aide-memory init` today get rules-only — no hook automation, no MCP tools surfaced. Compare to Claude Code which gets `.claude/settings.json` (hooks for SessionStart/PreCompact/Stop/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse with matchers Read/Edit/Write/Grep/Glob + 5 aide-memory MCP tools) + `.mcp.json` (aide-memory server registration).

Cursor hook event names inferred from the stale on-disk file (needs confirmation from research agent + Cursor docs):
- `stop` → Claude Code's `Stop`
- `beforeSubmitPrompt` → `UserPromptSubmit`
- `beforeReadFile` → `PreToolUse` matcher=Read
- Schema shape: `{ "version": 1, "hooks": { "<event>": [{ "command": "...", "type": "command", "timeout": N }] } }`
- Unknown equivalents: pre-edit, pre-search, pre-compact, session-start — research agent validating.

Downstream work planned in `docs/specs/CURSOR_ONBOARDING.md` (to be created): add CursorAdapter to a new EditorAdapter interface that abstracts per-editor init file generation. Each adapter owns its editor's rule-file template, hook-config shape, MCP-config shape. Adding Windsurf/Codex/Cline/Aider/etc. later becomes a 1-file adapter + registration. Also: restructure MANUAL_E2E_VALIDATION.md into per-editor matrix (Claude Code column + Cursor column) so every validation scenario covers both editors. Unblocks PHASE_0_1_SPEC P1.9 (Cursor Validation) + P1.17 (5 scenarios in Cursor) which have been DEFERRED.
why: Core product-gap finding — future sessions reading init.ts need to know the file generation is Claude-Code-first and Cursor-incomplete. Without this memory someone scanning init.ts sees the rules.mdc write and might reasonably assume "Cursor support is done" without realizing hooks + MCP aren't generated. Also captures the hook-event-name mapping inferred from the legacy on-disk file, saving a grep next time someone works on Cursor onboarding.
